newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - November 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - November 4.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Monday.

- A fast track for Sinn Fein into all-party talks, but with a delay on the start of substantive negotiations, is believed to be a key element in a deal SDLP leader John Hume and the Irish government hope may salvage the peace process.

- Reconciliation in Northern Ireland was not something to be attempted only after a political solution has been found, the new Catholic Primate and Archbishop of Armagh, Sean Brady, said at his installation on Sunday.
- Parents should sign a guarantee that their children will observe a code of behaviour at school, according to new proposals from the Teachers' Union of Ireland.

- The Irish pound is likely to come under renewed downward pressure from sterling over the next few days and dealers believe that the Central Bank will continue to buy Ireland's currency to try and keep it above parity against sterling.
- John Hume, leader of the Social Democratic Labour Party, emerged on Sunday as the key figure in moves to secure a new ceasefire by the Irish Republican Army.
- Irish police are hunting murdered gang boss Martin Cahill's brother who escaped from a police van on Dublin's Naas Road on Sunday by threatening prison officers with a syringe.

- Irish building society savers and borrowers could share a bonanza of around 650 million punts if the three societies, First National, Educational Building Society and Irish Nationwide, were to follow the Irish Permanent to the stock market.
